sources.title: Tonga Second Nationally Determined Contributions Review Report
sources.organization: Government of Tonga, Department of Climate Change (MEIDECC)
sources.temporal_coverage: Government review of NDC 2.0 implementation; includes 2020-2023 measures and earlier studies with projections to about 2090 and 2100.
sources.methodology: Government review of NDC implementation and sector evidence; estimates also cite earlier studies.
sources.limitations: Evidence vintages vary; projections cite earlier studies, and mangrove effectiveness is unquantified.

sources.title: Kingdom of Tonga Technology Needs Assessment Adaptation Report
sources.organization: Department of Energy, Government of Tonga; GEF-funded UNEP Technology Needs Assessment with UNEP-CCC and University of the South Pacific support
sources.temporal_coverage: Adaptation technology-needs assessment prepared in December 2023; includes water-risk data and citations from 2019-2021.
sources.methodology: Government-led review and stakeholder prioritization for agriculture and water technologies.
sources.limitations: Risk estimates cite older studies; priorities and proposed support are not evaluated results.

sources.title: Innovative Approaches to Water Resilience in Tonga
sources.organization: United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction and Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure
sources.temporal_coverage: Reports on water-sector workshops in November 2023 and a stakeholder roundtable on 10 May 2024.
sources.methodology: UNDRR account of stakeholder consultation on water infrastructure resilience.
sources.limitations: Consultation recommendations are not completed works or measured local resilience outcomes.

sources.title: Climate Resilient Islands
sources.temporal_coverage: The project page describes a six-year 2021-2026 programme.
sources.methodology: Implementer webpage summarizing programme design, locations and planned activities.
sources.limitations: The page does not report completion or evaluated outcomes; participant and household figures are programme targets.

sources.title: Two Years on, the Tonga Tsunami Shows Effective Risk Communication Saves Lives
sources.organization: United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction
sources.temporal_coverage: Retrospective account of preparedness and response to the 15 January 2022 volcanic eruption and tsunami; follow-up reported in January 2024.
sources.methodology: UNDRR retrospective using community and government accounts of warning and evacuation.
sources.limitations: The event was volcanic and tsunami-related, not a climate-attributed hazard; the article is not an impact evaluation.

claims.locator: Printed p. 56, section 4.2.1, coastal-protection implementation status.
claims.paraphrase: The government review reports current coastal flooding in low-lying Popua and Sopu; Sopu wetlands buffer high tides by about 30 cm, but the protection is weakening as seas rise.
institutions: Government of Tonga, Department of Climate Change
claims.limitations: The review cites earlier studies for some coastal estimates; wetland buffering is not a quantified loss-reduction evaluation.

claims.locator: Printed p. 56, section 4.2.1, Nuku'alofa high-tide inundation paragraph citing ADB (2019).
claims.paraphrase: A 2025 review summarizes an ADB (2019) projection that by about 2090 high tides may inundate low-lying Nuku'alofa, possibly forcing residential-area abandonment.
claims.scenario: Scenario is unspecified in the ADB (2019) summary.
institutions: Government of Tonga, Department of Climate Change
claims.limitations: This is a government review's summary of a 2019 projection, not a new local model or observed outcome.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 55-57, coastal-planting and monitoring discussion, including Sopu.
claims.paraphrase: Tonga's 2020-2023 One Million Trees initiative planted mostly mangroves; the review says it may have strengthened coastal resilience, but land saved is unquantified and Sopu's wetland buffer may be shrinking.
institutions: Government of Tonga, Department of Climate Change
claims.limitations: The review explicitly says shoreline and mangrove monitoring is insufficient to measure land saved or protection impact.

claims.locator: Printed p. 26, section 4.1, outer-island water vulnerability discussion citing DFAT (2021) and Tonga government data (2019).
claims.paraphrase: The assessment identifies drought and possible groundwater salinization on low-lying Ha'apai islands; some remote Ha'apai and Vava'u islands rely solely on rainwater and face rainfall variation.
geographies: small remote islands in Ha'apai and Vava'u
affected_groups: residents of low-lying and remote islands
institutions: Department of Energy, Government of Tonga
claims.limitations: The assessment cites partner and government data from 2019-2021; it does not give island-specific household counts.

claims.locator: Printed p. 19, section 3.1, agriculture vulnerability discussion citing Government of Tonga (2019).
claims.paraphrase: The assessment cites a 2019 government estimate that 208 km², or 39% of Tonga's total land area, was drought-vulnerable, with higher proportions in Tongatapu and Vava'u.
institutions: Department of Energy, Government of Tonga
claims.limitations: The 208 km² and 39% denominator apply nationally; no island-specific area or denominator is supplied.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 45-46, community water-supply support factsheet, `Endorsement by experts', `Adequacy for current climate' and `Status'.
claims.paraphrase: Village water committees manage rural and outer-island supplies; the assessment says community systems are more weather-exposed than utility systems and need support to prepare for drought.
geographies: rural villages and remote outer islands in Tonga
claims.limitations: Needs assessment only; committee performance and delivered support were not evaluated.

claims.locator: Article paragraphs on the 10 May 2024 water roundtable and proposed initial actions.
claims.paraphrase: Stakeholders identified Tonga's water sector as highly vulnerable and proposed better groundwater monitoring, village water-committee training and wider use of spatial data in planning and vulnerability assessment.
claims.limitations: This records workshop discussion and initial recommendations, not delivered training or tested changes in water resilience.

claims.locator: Project page, `Project Background' and `Our Work' paragraphs.
claims.paraphrase: Live & Learn describes a 2021-2026 programme across 15 communities in Ha'apai (4), Vava'u (8) and 'Eua (3), targeting community plans, nature-based actions, training for 20 representatives and direct actions for 20 households per site.
claims.limitations: Implementer-reported programme design; the page does not state completion or verify that target participants and households were reached.

claims.locator: Article paragraphs describing evacuation warnings, traditional knowledge and the 2022 response.
claims.paraphrase: During the 2022 volcanic tsunami, communities used radio, word-of-mouth and inherited hazard knowledge to move people inland or to high ground; UNDRR reports four deaths despite widespread impact.
claims.limitations: This was a geophysical disaster, not a climate-attributed event; the article does not evaluate differential outcomes by village or group.

access_audit.locator: Complete 98-page government review; coastal protection and NDC implementation sections, printed pp. 55-57.
access_audit.notes: Local risk passages include Popua and Sopu; the Nuku'alofa 2090 estimate is attributed to ADB (2019).
access_audit.reuse_terms: No separate open licence verified; concise attributed paraphrases only.

access_audit.locator: Complete 53-page adaptation report; printed pp. 19, 26 and 45-46.
access_audit.notes: Water and drought evidence cites older partner or government materials; recommendations are distinguished from delivered outcomes.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Report permits educational and nonprofit reproduction with attribution; concise attributed paraphrases only.

access_audit.locator: Full article, dated 13 May 2024, on water-sector consultations and initial actions.
access_audit.notes: Recommendations are attributed to consultation participants.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No separate open licence verified; concise attributed paraphrases only.

access_audit.locator: Full programme page, including project locations, stated 2021-2026 duration and target activities.
access_audit.notes: The 15-community distribution and participation figures are programme descriptions/targets, not independently verified outcomes.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No separate open licence verified; concise attributed paraphrases only.

access_audit.locator: Full UNDRR retrospective, 15 January 2024, sections on public awareness and evacuation response.
access_audit.notes: The cited 2022 event is volcanic/tsunami-related rather than climate-attributed.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No separate open licence verified; concise attributed paraphrases only.

access_audit.locator: A 17.05 MB community-profile PDF linked from the directly read landing page.
access_audit.notes: The linked PDF could not be opened by the web reader; no PDF-only findings were used. The landing page itself was read and is separately recorded as TON-SRC-104.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Not assessed for the inaccessible PDF.

search_audit.query: Tonga climate change subnational coastal erosion flooding islands Ha'apai Vava'u government primary source
search_audit.outcome: Read government NDC and adaptation reports with named-site coastal flooding in Popua/Sopu, a projected Nuku'alofa inundation pathway and outer-island water/drought differentiation. Some underlying estimates are older and are attributed in the claims.

search_audit.query: Tonga climate change conflict land water resource disputes drought cyclone social cohesion primary report
search_audit.outcome: The inspected climate/adaptation sources discuss water vulnerability and capacity needs but did not provide a source-stated pathway from a climate hazard through insecurity, violence, displacement or conflict in Tonga. This is an evidence gap, not evidence that no such pathway exists.

search_audit.query: Tonga disaster conflict insecurity violence blocked climate adaptation response access island report
search_audit.outcome: No inspected source documented violence or insecurity blocking a named climate-adaptation activity or climate response. The evidence reviewed describes hazard exposure, water institutions and disaster response, not an FCV-to-climate pathway.

search_audit.query: Tonga community climate resilience water village committees outer islands 2024 2025 report
search_audit.outcome: Found village water-committee support needs, a stakeholder proposal for groundwater monitoring and spatial planning, and an implementer-described community programme across Ha'apai, Vava'u and 'Eua. Separately, UNDRR reports community warning and evacuation capacity during the non-climate 2022 tsunami.

gaps: No inspected public source stated a climate-to-conflict, violence, displacement or insecurity mediator for Tonga; this records a search gap rather than national absence.
No inspected source documented insecurity or violence directly constraining a named adaptation operation or climate response.
The Nuku'alofa high-tide inundation estimate is reported through a 2025 government review citing ADB (2019); the underlying scenario is unspecified in the summary.
The TNA's outer-island water and drought estimates rely partly on 2019-2021 sources, and the national drought-vulnerable land percentage is not disaggregated by island.
The Live & Learn page reports programme design and targets, not verified completion or evaluated resilience outcomes; the linked community-profile PDF was not accessible.
